name: Kernex Microsystems (India) Ltd
tagline: Kavach/TCAS order book (Rs 3,487 Cr) now backed by a Q1 FY27 print where quarterly revenue (Rs 504 Cr) exceeded all of FY26; trailing P/E ~15x and ~7x on FY27 execution, but 268 debtor days and a low, drifting-down promoter stake keep earnings quality in question
business_overview: Kernex -- train collision avoidance system (TCAS/Kavach) manufacturer, riding India's mandated railway safety rollout. Effectively a single-customer (Indian Railways / production units CLW, ICF, BLW, PLW) tender business; one of ~4-5 RDSO-approved Kavach OEMs alongside HBL Engineering, Medha, Siemens and others.
fundamentals_table: Rs 2,914 Cr (price ~Rs 1,734; off the Rs 1,918 52-wk high, mcap down from ~Rs 3,305 Cr at prior pass)
ROE ~43.5% / ROCE ~47.8% (latest FY; 5-yr average ROCE still negative ~-12% -- this is a recent turnaround, not a proven compounder)
Total-liabilities/equity ~2.7x; interest cost rising through FY26; working-capital funded (debtor days ~268)
FY25 Rs 191 Cr -> FY26 Rs 430 Cr (+125%); Q1 FY27 revenue Rs 504 Cr alone (> all of FY26). 3-yr sales CAGR ~374%; TTM profit growth ~253%
P/E ~15.3x trailing, ~11.7x book (BV ~Rs 148); ~7x on an indicative FY27 PAT if ~Rs 2,100 Cr order execution holds
fundamentals_narrative: Q1 FY27 materially de-risked the execution question: revenue Rs 503.6 Cr (vs Rs 59.9 Cr in Q1 FY26), EBITDA ~Rs 163 Cr at 32.3% margin (vs 22.5%), PAT Rs 109.85 Cr (vs Rs 7.4 Cr) -- a single quarter larger than all of FY26. Outstanding order book is Rs 3,487 Cr with management guiding ~Rs 2,100 Cr executable in FY27, against a Rs 2,914 Cr market cap. On trailing FY26 numbers (revenue Rs 430 Cr, PAT Rs 88 Cr, EPS ~Rs 52.6) the stock is ~15x earnings; on FY27 execution it is closer to ~7x. The offsets are real and unresolved: debtor days ~268 mean reported profit is not converting to cash, the 'supplied vs installed & commissioned' revenue-recognition timing question remains open, promoter holding is low and declining (~28.7%), there is no dividend despite the profit surge, and leverage/interest cost are rising. The 5-year average ROCE is still negative -- this is a turnaround riding a policy mandate, priced as though the mandate is certain.
technical_read: Not independently pulled. Stock has de-rated from the Rs 1,918 high to ~Rs 1,734; market wants order-book continuity, cash conversion and diversification beyond Kavach before assigning a higher multiple (HBL Engineering's re-rating struggle cited in-thread as the cautionary parallel).
sentiment_summary: Read the most recent 50 of 256 posts (2025-11 to 2026-08). A community member investigated management remuneration (raised alongside sales/profit growth) and concluded the absolute amounts (Rs 25-40 lakh p.a.) were reasonable versus industry, not a governance concern. Stock fell on Q1 FY27 results despite headline strength -- community attributes this to the market wanting to see order-book continuity and diversification beyond Kavach before assigning a higher multiple (citing HBL Engineering's current re-rating struggle as a cautionary parallel).
community_signal: kartik_bhat (trusted, elevated) posted a detailed, order-by-order breakdown (Aug 18, 2026): total outstanding order book Rs 3,641 Cr, of which the CLW order is 45% complete (Rs 1,300 Cr balance), and remaining execution timeline implies ~Rs 2,800-2,900 Cr FY27 topline -- against a Rs 3,305 Cr market cap, this is a genuinely cheap forward multiple if execution holds. A countervailing, technically valid point from another poster: revenue recognition may be based on 'supplied' rather than 'installed & commissioned' units, which could overstate near-term completion.

verdict_headline: Order book now validated by a step-change quarter and the stock is cheap on forward execution -- but cash conversion, revenue-recognition timing and a low/declining promoter stake keep conviction at Medium
verdict_reasoning: Q1 FY27 (a single quarter larger than all of FY26, 32% EBITDA margin) is a real live inflection: on the small/mid-cap recent-trajectory rule, tailwind and TAM read 'yes' and four_box reaches 3.0, so the 10x-in-2-3-years label is permitted

Conviction held at Medium (not raised) because the earnings quality is genuinely unresolved: ~268 debtor days, the open 'supplied vs commissioned' revenue-recognition question, no dividend, rising leverage, and a promoter stake that is both low (~28.7%) and drifting down
Re-rating trigger: two consecutive quarters of order execution WITH visible receivables collection / operating cash flow, plus any diversification of the customer base beyond Indian Railways
notes_short: Kavach/TCAS order book Rs 3,487cr (~Rs 2,100cr executable FY27) vs Rs 2,914cr mcap; Q1 FY27 revenue Rs 504cr > all FY26, 32% EBITDA margin; ~15x trailing / ~7x forward P/E. Offsets: 268 debtor days, rev-rec timing question, promoter 28.7% & falling, no dividend.

open_questions: Is revenue recognised on 'supplied' or on 'installed & commissioned' units -- and how large is the gap between reported completion % and cash-backed completion?
Will receivables (268 days) actually be collected, and when does operating cash flow turn clearly positive?
Does the customer base ever diversify beyond Indian Railways production units, or is this permanently a single-buyer tender business?
Why is the promoter stake drifting down during the biggest up-cycle in the company's history?
deep_dive.conviction_update: Medium -> Medium. Q1 FY27 removed most of the execution doubt (a quarter bigger than all of FY26, 32% EBITDA margin) and the stock is now cheap on forward numbers, but ~268 debtor days, the open revenue-recognition timing question, no dividend and a low/declining promoter stake are enough to hold rather than raise conviction.

earnings_chain.operating_leverage: yes -- EBITDA margin jumped 22.5% -> 32.3% YoY as revenue scaled on a largely fixed cost base

market_expectation.implied_growth_cagr: At ~15x trailing with a ~14x cyclical/tender-business exit multiple, the market is implying roughly flat-to-modest EPS growth from the FY26 base -- i.e. it is NOT extrapolating the Q1 FY27 run-rate
market_expectation.our_fy27_estimate: Revenue Rs 1,800-2,100 Cr on order execution; EBITDA margin high-20s to ~30%; PAT Rs 300-420 Cr if collection/commissioning hold -- forward P/E ~7-10x
market_expectation.our_fy28_estimate: Depends entirely on order-book replenishment; base case revenue holds Rs 1,500-2,000 Cr if Kavach award cadence continues, downside sharp if awards pause
market_expectation.gap_basis: Q1 FY27 quarterly revenue already exceeded FY26 full-year; trailing P/E of ~15x does not reflect the order-book-backed FY27 execution path. Gap is discounted heavily for cash-conversion and revenue-recognition-timing risk
market_expectation.data_caveat: no broker consensus; implied path is a reverse-P/E estimate + screener.in forward figures + VP thread view

catalyst.event: A Q2/Q3 FY27 print showing sustained execution WITH visible receivables collection / positive operating cash flow (plus continued Kavach award cadence)

value_chain.theme: Indian railway safety / automatic train protection (Kavach/TCAS)
value_chain.position: RDSO-approved Kavach OEM supplying trackside + loco equipment to Railway production units
value_chain.bottleneck_node: RDSO approval + field testing/commissioning capacity across the network
value_chain.note: Supply side is adding capacity (multiple approved OEMs scaling for the same mandated rollout); tender-driven awards mean pricing power sits with Indian Railways, not the vendors. Approval + installed base give some stickiness but each new tranche is competitively bid.

drivers: operating leverage on a fixed cost base as execution volume scaled
favourable order mix in the current execution phase
earnings_quality.normalised_note: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin of 32.3% is well above any defensible through-cycle level for a Railway tender-supply business; part of the lift is genuine operating leverage but part is current-phase mix and low base. A mid-20s% through-cycle margin is more defensible. Cash conversion (268 debtor days) further separates reported margin from economic margin.

growth_trajectory.last_quarters_note: YoY revenue growth oldest->newest is dominated by low-base and order-execution timing: FY25 +~130%, FY26 +125%, Q1 FY27 +740% YoY (Rs 60 Cr -> Rs 504 Cr). This is order/project execution, not a smooth demand ramp -- treat as lumpy
growth_trajectory.reverse_pe_note: ~15x trailing needs only modest EPS growth off FY26 to be fair at a ~14x tender-business exit; the FY27 execution path implies far more, but replenishment risk beyond FY27-28 caps how much of that is durable

management_quality.capital_allocation: All FY26 cash retained into working capital and execution (no dividend); incremental capital is earning a high ROCE in the current phase but the 5-yr average ROCE is negative, so the reinvestment track record is short. No unrelated diversification observed

quality_metrics.open_questions: FCF conversion could not be reliably sourced for a clean trailing-3y average, but directionally very weak -- 268 debtor days and no dividend indicate reported PAT is not converting to cash; net-debt/EBITDA screens low only because the current EBITDA base is inflated by the execution spike

track_record.note: Of FY24/FY25/FY26, only FY26 (and arguably FY25 on the low base) clearly cleared BOTH revenue growth >=10% AND ROCE >=15% in the same year -- prior years were loss-making / sub-scale. FY26 is the one unambiguous pass; FY25 borderline. This is a 1-2 year turnaround, not a consistent compounder.

four_box.note: tailwind yes (mandated multi-year Kavach rollout, only a fraction of the network covered). tam yes on the small-cap live-inflection rule -- Q1 FY27 revenue alone exceeded all of FY26 and the Rs 3,487 Cr order book exceeds the Rs 2,914 Cr mcap. moat weak (tender-driven, 4-5 approved OEMs, pricing power sits with Indian Railways). valuation weak (~15x trailing / ~7x forward looks cheap, but 11.7x book and 268 debtor days mean reported earnings quality is suspect -- not a clean 'yes'). Score 3.0 -> 10x-in-2-3-years permitted; conviction still held at Medium on earnings-quality grounds.
